name: application-survey-progress-header
title: Survey Progress Header
description: "Question X of N" label and progress fill computed from real position/total props, with Back/Next controls that disable and relabel at the survey boundaries.
useWhen: Heading a single-question-at-a-time survey or quiz flow where only overall position matters, not named step labels.
The number of questions is large or dynamic, making a labeled per-step indicator (like a numbered stepper) impractical.
You want the Back button and Next/Submit label to automatically reflect whether the respondent is at the first or last question.
avoidWhen: Steps have distinct names the user should see (Account, Profile, Review) — use `multi-step-progress` for that labeled-step stepper instead.
There's no linear position to track — a plain progress bar without question framing is enough.
The flow allows jumping to arbitrary questions — pair this with a dedicated question navigator instead of relying on Back/Next alone.
responsiveBehavior: Fixed-width card (max-w-lg) with a full-width progress bar; label and percentage text wrap rather than overflowing at narrow widths.
accessibility: The progress bar's fill percentage and the visible '% complete' text are both derived from the same currentQuestion/totalQuestions props.
The Back button is a real disabled <button> at the first question rather than just visually dimmed, and the Next button relabels to 'Submit' at the last question based on the same boundary check.
Question position is announced as real text ('Question 3 of 8'), not conveyed by the progress bar alone.

variants.title: Survey Progress Header
variants.description: Question 3 of 8, 37% complete, Back enabled and Next showing (not yet at the last question).
accessibility: Progress fill and '% complete' text are computed from the same currentQuestion/totalQuestions values; Back disables and Next relabels from the same boundary checks.

variants.title: Survey Progress Header (Dark)
variants.description: Survey progress header adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Progress bar and button colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
